note: THERMAL efficiency of state-of-the-art dry kilns with heat recovery (about 63%); 'through integrated approaches could reach 80%' (ref 60). Over 85% of kilns worldwide use dry methods. The 80% is a potential, recorded as the max; no min given.

value: modern dry-process clinker kiln with preheater/precalciner and heat recovery; highly flexible on fuel - many European plants use waste streams for more than 80% of their energy. Fuel is now only about one third of clinker CO2, the rest being limestone decarbonation

limestone calcined clay cement (LC3): clinker partly replaced by calcined clay (heated to relatively modest temperatures) plus limestone, with good performance at high substitution levels; not limited by SCM availability as fly ash and slag are

note: 'overall CO2 savings of 15-30% of current levels from cement, can be achieved worldwide' - a sector-wide potential from substituting clinker with calcined clay and limestone, not a per-tonne product saving
